AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: Sigmoid volvulus is a condition with a tendency to recur if treated conservatively. Little is known about the type or when to perform definitive surgery. The aim of this study was to review treatment, and asses the outcome, of sigmoid volvulus in adult patients treated at a Swedish university hospital.

AbstractText.Label: METHOD
AbstractText.content: The medical records of patients treated for sigmoid volvulus at Sahlgrenska University Hospital from January 2000 to September 2016 were reviewed retrospectively. Median follow-up time was 8.3 years.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: One hundred and sixty-eight patients were included with a total of 453 admissions for sigmoid volvulus. Non-operative decompression was attempted as initial treatment in 438/453 (97%) with a success rate of 92% (403/438) and was not influenced by whether it was the first episode or a recurrence. Without planned surgery, recurrence occurred after 84% of successful non-operative decompressions (median of two recurrences (1-16). Recurrence was less common after the first episode compared to subsequent episodes. Median time until recurrence was 58 days. Mortality after planned surgery following successful decompression was 3.3% (2/61) compared to 13% (6/46) following emergency surgery.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: In our cohort, the recurrence rate of sigmoid volvulus following successful non-operative decompression was high. Still, more than 20% of patients did not experience a recurrence after their first episode. Non-operative decompression could thus be suggested as the sole treatment for the first episode of volvulus. However, after the second episode it is probable that early planned surgery would improve outcome and reduce health care consumption. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
